definition: Hedonist means one who believes pleasure should be the primary pursuit of humans.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word hedonist. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know hedonist should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Casio the cat lives as a shameless hedonist, migrating around the house all day to occupy whichever patch of sunlight is warmest.
A fun-lover is milder than a hedonist: happy to take pleasure when it arrives, never reorganizing life around it.
A bon vivant savors good living — fine tables, good company — but stops short of the hedonist's full creed that pleasure is the point of everything.

A pleasure-seeker is anyone out chasing enjoyment — a single indulgent weekend earns the plain compound. A hedonist is a pleasure-seeker with a philosophy: pleasure is not one pursuit among many but the measure every choice must answer to. The seeking can be casual; the hedonism is a creed.

A sybarite is devoted to luxury — silk, spas, long baths, fine rooms — pleasure pursued through expense and comfort. A hedonist needs no money at all: the creed is only that pleasure, cheap or costly, is the point of a life. Sybarite names the taste; hedonist names the philosophy.

The word can be a philosophy-classroom term or a raised eyebrow, depending on who is saying it.
Hedonist is the label for someone whose compass points at pleasure — as philosophy or lifestyle.
A sybarite luxuriates, a glutton overeats, an epicure savors selectively; the hedonist outranks them all, because for him pleasure isn't a hobby but the whole point.
His opposite number, the ascetic, renounces exactly what he enshrines.

On the morning she retired, Gran taped a handwritten notice to her refrigerator: 'This household now runs on delight.' She meant it as policy, not as a joke.
Breakfast moved to the porch for the light; errands were rerouted past the duck pond; any chore that could not be made pleasant was examined for whether it needed doing at all.
Her sister calls it laziness.
Gran corrects her: laziness avoids effort, while she will happily haul fifty pounds of compost for the roses.
'A hedonist,' she says, 'is just someone honest about the point of a life.' The point, in her accounting, is joy — cheap joy, mostly, since the pension is small.
Visitors leave with cuttings from the roses and, sometimes, with the suspicion that she is onto something.
